source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

chapters.title: Natural Resources and Their Use
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: When does Nature become a Resource?
objectives: Student can explain that parts of Nature become resources when humans use them
Student can explain that a resource must be technologically accessible, economically feasible and culturally acceptable
visualIdeas: a tree in a forest beside the same wood made into furniture

topics.title: Categories of Natural Resources
objectives: Student can explain why we categorise things using shared criteria
Student can group natural resources into resources essential for life, for materials and for energy
visualIdeas: three baskets labelled life, materials and energy with resources sorted into them

topics.title: Renewable and Non-renewable Resources
objectives: Student can distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources with examples
Student can explain how Nature restores and regenerates itself and how overuse can make a renewable resource scarce
visualIdeas: a forest regrowing after a fire beside a coal mine running out

topics.title: Distribution of Natural Resources and its Implications
objectives: Student can explain that natural resources are unevenly distributed across the world and within India
Student can explain how this shapes settlements, trade, international relations and conflicts
Student can read a map showing where coal, oil, iron ore and bauxite are found in India
visualIdeas: a map of India marking coal, oil, iron ore and bauxite sites

topics.title: The 'Paradox of Plenty'
objectives: Student can explain the resource curse: having plenty of natural resources does not by itself make a country rich
Student can explain how investing in industries, technology and skills helps avoid it
visualIdeas: a resource-rich region with raw materials leaving and finished goods coming back

topics.title: Responsible and Wise Use of Natural Resources: Stewardship
objectives: Student can explain stewardship as using resources so that renewables regenerate and non-renewables last
Student can describe how overuse of groundwater in Punjab and of chemical fertilisers harms resources
Student can describe responses such as less polluting building materials and organic farming in Sikkim
visualIdeas: a depth-to-water map of Punjab
an organic terrace farm in Sikkim

topics.title: Responsible and Judicious Use of Resources
objectives: Student can explain why non-renewables should be used judiciously while switching to renewable energy
Student can describe India's role in the International Solar Alliance and solar parks like Bhadla
Student can explain that access to clean water and air is often unfair to some sections of society
visualIdeas: a satellite view of a large solar park in Rajasthan

chapters.title: Reshaping India's Political Map
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: The Medieval Period and New Invasions
objectives: Student can explain how the textbook uses the term medieval for the 11th to 17th centuries in India
Student can describe the invasions from beyond the Hindu Kush that reshaped India's political map from the 11th century
Student can read the chapter timeline from the Delhi Sultanate to the Sikh Empire
visualIdeas: a timeline from 1206 to 1799 with key battles and dynasties

topics.title: Rise and Fall of the Delhi Sultanate
objectives: Student can name the five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate
Student can describe the political instability, violent successions and military campaigns of the period, including Ala-ud-din Khilji's campaigns and his repulsion of Mongol invasions
Student can explain how the Sultanate weakened, including Timur's attack on Delhi
visualIdeas: a map of the Delhi Sultanate with neighbouring kingdoms like the Eastern Gangas and Hoysalas

topics.title: Resistance to the Delhi Sultanate
objectives: Student can describe kingdoms that resisted the Sultanate, such as the Eastern Gangas under Narasimhadeva I
Student can connect the Konark Surya temple with these victories
visualIdeas: the Konark Surya temple with its stone wheels

topics.title: The Vijayanagara Empire
objectives: Student can describe how Harihara and Bukka founded the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century
Student can describe the empire's peak under Krishnadevaraya and his patronage of literature and temples
Student can explain how the Battle of Talikota in 1565 led to the destruction of Vijayanagara city
visualIdeas: ruins of Hampi with the Virupaksha temple

topics.title: The Mughals: Babur and Akbar
objectives: Student can explain how Babur's victory at Panipat in 1526 founded the Mughal Empire
Student can describe Akbar's reign as a blend of brutality and tolerance, including the siege of Chittor and his later policies
visualIdeas: the battle of Panipat as painted in the Baburnama, showing cannons

topics.title: Aurangzeb
objectives: Student can describe how Aurangzeb came to the throne and expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest extent
Student can explain how long Deccan wars and rebellions strained the empire
visualIdeas: a map of the Mughal Empire at its largest around 1700

topics.title: Resistance to the Mughals
objectives: Student can describe peasant and tribal resistance to Mughal rule, such as the Jats, Bhils, Gonds and Santhals
Student can describe the resistance of the Rajputs, including Maharana Pratap at Haldighati
visualIdeas: an artist's impression of the Battle of Haldighati

topics.title: The Ahoms and the Rise of the Sikhs
objectives: Student can describe the Ahom kingdom, its paik system and its victory over the Mughals at Saraighat
Student can describe how the Sikh Gurus responded to persecution, the formation of the Khalsa in 1699 and the later Sikh Empire
visualIdeas: a map of the Brahmaputra valley and of Punjab with the Ahom and Sikh territories

topics.title: Administering India
objectives: Student can describe the Delhi Sultanate's administration and its iqta system
Student can describe Akbar's administrative framework, including provinces (subahs) and the mansabdari system
visualIdeas: a chart of Mughal ministers: Diwan, Mir Bakhshi, Khan-i-Saman and Sadr

topics.title: People's Lives
objectives: Student can describe the economy of the period: agriculture, artisans, guilds (shrenis), trade networks and coinage
Student can explain that India remained wealthy while the condition of common people was often harsh
visualIdeas: a busy market with weavers, traders and coins of the period

chapters.title: The Rise of the Marathas
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Who are the Marathas?
objectives: Student can identify the Marathas as a people of the Deccan, especially present-day Maharashtra, identified with the Marathi language
Student can describe the region's history before the rise of Maratha power
visualIdeas: a map of the Deccan plateau with Maharashtra highlighted

topics.title: Foundation of Maratha Power and the Rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji
objectives: Student can describe Chhatrapati Shivaji's early life and his campaigns against the Deccan sultanates and the Mughals
Student can explain the role of forts and of his coronation in founding the Maratha kingdom
visualIdeas: Raigad and other forts of Chhatrapati Shivaji marked on a map

topics.title: The Marathas after Chhatrapati Shivaji
objectives: Student can describe the Mughal-Maratha conflict under Sambhaji, Rajaram and Tarabai
Student can describe the 18th-century expansion of Maratha power across India under the Peshwas
visualIdeas: a map of Maratha territory expanding across India in the 18th century

topics.title: Maratha Administration
objectives: Student can describe Chhatrapati Shivaji's civilian administration, including salaried officials instead of hereditary posts
Student can describe the Maratha military, navy under Kanhoji Angre, judicial system and trade networks
visualIdeas: Maratha ships challenging European ships off India's west coast

topics.title: Cultural Revival
objectives: Student can explain how Chhatrapati Shivaji promoted Sanskrit and Marathi, for example through his seal and the Rajya-Vyavahara-Kosha
Student can describe the roles of Maratha women such as Tarabai and Ahilyabai Holkar
visualIdeas: Chhatrapati Shivaji's Sanskrit seal

topics.title: In focus: Thanjavur and the Maratha Legacy
objectives: Student can describe Maratha patronage of the arts in Thanjavur
Student can explain the Maratha legacy and the ideal of Swarajya
visualIdeas: a Thanjavur painting with gold foil work

chapters.title: The Colonial Era in India
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: The Age of Colonialism
objectives: Student can define colonialism
Student can explain why European powers sought colonies
visualIdeas: a world map with European sea routes to Asia, Africa and the Americas

topics.title: Europeans in India: Portuguese, Dutch and French
objectives: Student can explain why India's wealth attracted European traders
Student can describe the Portuguese, Dutch and French presence in India and how their aims differed
visualIdeas: a map of Portuguese, Dutch and French trading posts in India

topics.title: Enter the British: From Traders to Rulers
objectives: Student can explain how the English East India Company turned from a trading company into a ruling power
Student can explain why the Battle of Plassey was a turning point for the Company
visualIdeas: a timeline from the Company's charter to its control of Bengal

topics.title: From Paradise to Hell?
objectives: Student can describe how Company revenue policies contributed to devastating famines such as the Bengal famine of 1770
Student can explain the idea of the drain of India's wealth

topics.title: Changing Landscapes
objectives: Student can explain the decline of India's indigenous industries such as textiles
Student can describe how traditional governance and education were dismantled and reshaped
Student can explain how the railways were designed to serve imperial needs
visualIdeas: handlooms falling silent beside bales of British mill cloth
a railway map leading from the interior to ports

topics.title: Early Resistance Movements: Challenging Colonial Authority
objectives: Student can describe early resistance such as the Sannyasi-Fakir rebellion
Student can describe tribal uprisings and peasant uprisings such as the Indigo Revolt
visualIdeas: indigo fields with peasants refusing to sow

topics.title: The Great Rebellion of 1857
objectives: Student can explain why historians call the events of 1857 the Great Rebellion rather than the Sepoy Mutiny
Student can describe the spread of the rebellion and how it was repressed
Student can describe the roles of leaders such as Rani Lakshmibai and Tatia Tope
visualIdeas: a map of the main centres of the 1857 rebellion

topics.title: The Legacy of European Colonialism in India
objectives: Student can explain why the textbook says colonial rule was not a civilising mission
Student can describe the lasting effects of colonial rule on India
visualIdeas: a two-column chart of colonial claims and their effects on India

chapters.title: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Universal Adult Franchise
objectives: Student can explain universal adult franchise: every citizen aged 18 and above has one vote of equal value
Student can explain why the Constitution makers adopted it from the start
visualIdeas: a queue of voters of different ages, genders and backgrounds each holding one ballot

topics.title: Bridging Barriers, Enabling Participation: Ensuring Universal Franchise
objectives: Student can explain the challenges of organising elections in a large and diverse country
Student can describe measures that help every eligible voter take part
visualIdeas: a polling team carrying voting machines to a remote village

topics.title: Election for Class Representative
objectives: Student can follow the steps of a fair election through the school class representative example
Student can relate the steps to real elections
visualIdeas: a classroom ballot box with three candidates' names

topics.title: The Role of the Election Commission of India (ECI)
objectives: Student can describe the ECI as the Constitutional body that conducts elections
Student can describe how the ECI manages the electoral process
visualIdeas: a flow chart from announcement of elections to counting of votes

topics.title: Model Code of Conduct (MCC)
objectives: Student can explain the purpose of the Model Code of Conduct
Student can give examples of what parties and candidates may and may not do

topics.title: Understanding Elections in India: Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
objectives: Student can explain how members of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies are directly elected from constituencies

topics.title: Election to the Rajya Sabha
objectives: Student can explain indirect election of Rajya Sabha members by MLAs

topics.title: Election of the President and Vice President of India
objectives: Student can describe the electoral college that elects the President
Student can describe how the Vice President is elected and their role as chairperson of the Rajya Sabha
visualIdeas: a diagram of the electoral college made of MPs and MLAs

topics.title: Challenges and The Road Ahead
objectives: Student can identify challenges such as money power, candidates with criminal records and voter apathy

visualIdeas: a voter awareness poster

chapters.title: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 1

topics.title: Introduction to the Parliamentary System
objectives: Student can explain how the Constitution set up a parliamentary system of government

topics.title: Legislative Functions of the Parliament: Constitutional Functions and Lawmaking
objectives: Student can describe Parliament's constitutional functions, such as electing the President and amending the Constitution

objectives: Student can explain how Parliament holds the executive accountable through questions and debates

visualIdeas: a question hour scene with a minister answering

topics.title: Executive Functions: The President, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
objectives: Student can explain that the President is the Head of State and the nominal head of the executive
Student can describe the role of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers in running the government
visualIdeas: an organisation chart from the President to the Prime Minister and ministries

topics.title: The Judiciary — Role of Checks and Balances
objectives: Student can explain the judiciary as the custodian of the Constitution
Student can explain how checks and balances keep each branch of government within its limits

topics.title: Legislative and Executive Functions at the State Level
objectives: Student can explain the Union, State and Concurrent Lists

topics.title: Challenges to the Effective Functioning of the Legislatures
objectives: Student can identify challenges such as disruptions and fewer sitting days

visualIdeas: a bar chart of sitting days of Parliament over the years

topics.title: Capital

topics.title: How are the Factors Connected?

topics.title: Responsibilities towards Factors of Production

topics.title: What are Rights?
objectives: Student can explain rights as justified claims needed to live with dignity, safety and respect
Student can explain why actions that harm others cannot be rights
visualIdeas: a set of rights cards: education, livelihood, expression

topics.title: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution
objectives: Student can name the six categories of Fundamental Rights with their Articles
Student can explain that Fundamental Rights protect people from unfair treatment by others and by the government
Student can explain that people can approach the courts if these rights are violated
visualIdeas: a wheel of the six Fundamental Rights with Article numbers

topics.title: Duties
objectives: Student can explain Fundamental Duties and when they were added to the Constitution
Student can give examples of Fundamental Duties from Article 51A
visualIdeas: a list of Fundamental Duties illustrated with everyday actions

topics.title: Rights and Duties: Two Sides of the Same Coin
objectives: Student can explain why rights and duties go together
Student can distinguish legally enforceable rights from moral and social duties
visualIdeas: a coin with rights on one face and duties on the other

topics.title: Discrimination
objectives: Student can define discrimination as unfair treatment based on identity
Student can distinguish visible and invisible discrimination using caselets
visualIdeas: two school caselets, one of name-calling and one of a child left out of a trip

topics.title: Inclusion
objectives: Student can explain inclusion as ensuring everyone feels welcomed and has equal access to opportunities
Student can suggest ways to make a school more inclusive
visualIdeas: a reading club with books in several languages

chapters.title: Dynamics of Population
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: What Is Demography?
objectives: Student can define demography as the study of the size, structure and changes of a population
Student can name the factors that change population: births, deaths and migration
visualIdeas: a diagram of births, deaths and migration flowing into and out of a population

topics.title: Population at a Glance
objectives: Student can state that India became the world's most populous country in 2023
Student can describe how world population has grown and is projected to change
visualIdeas: a bar graph of the world's most populous countries

topics.title: What Determines the Population of a Country?
objectives: Student can define birth rate, fertility rate and death rate
Student can explain replacement level fertility of 2.1
visualIdeas: a family tree showing replacement level fertility

topics.title: Death Rate and Migration
objectives: Student can explain how lower mortality and higher life expectancy reflect better healthcare
Student can explain why people migrate and its effects on cities
visualIdeas: a line graph of India's life expectancy rising from 30 to 70 years

topics.title: How Do Countries Experience Population Change?
objectives: Student can describe the stages of demographic transition
Student can explain why many developed countries have shrinking and ageing populations
visualIdeas: a demographic transition graph with birth and death rate curves

topics.title: India's Population: Composition and Trends
objectives: Student can describe the composition of India's population by age, gender and other characteristics
Student can read a population pyramid
visualIdeas: India's population pyramid

topics.title: India's Demographic Dividend — A Limited Window of Opportunity
objectives: Student can explain the demographic dividend and youth bulge
Student can explain why investing in education, health and jobs is needed before the window closes
visualIdeas: a bar chart of median age in India, Japan, China and the USA

chapters.title: India's Urban Landscape
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: Introduction to India's Urban Landscape
objectives: Student can describe India's urban legacy from Harappan cities to historical cities still flourishing today
Student can describe what makes an area a city today
visualIdeas: a timeline of Indian cities from Dholavira to modern metros

topics.title: Population Density in Cities
objectives: Student can define and calculate population density
Student can compare the density of different cities
visualIdeas: dots packed densely in a city grid beside sparse dots in a village

topics.title: How do Cities Become Centres of Economic Activities?
objectives: Student can explain how location near rivers and trade routes helped cities grow
Student can explain why a growing share of the world's population lives in cities
visualIdeas: a city growing at the crossing of a river and a trade route

topics.title: What Leads to Urbanisation?
objectives: Student can describe the stages by which a village becomes a town and then a metropolitan city
Student can explain how a shift to industry and services drives urbanisation
visualIdeas: a flow chart from rural origins to a metropolitan area

topics.title: Cities as Cultural Hubs
objectives: Student can explain how people from many regions mix in cities to create shared culture
Student can give examples such as Mumbai's vada pav and Kolkata's cultural institutions
visualIdeas: a street food stall surrounded by people from different regions

topics.title: Challenges Faced by Cities
objectives: Student can identify challenges such as pollution, traffic, slums, heat islands and waste
Student can explain how rapid growth strains urban infrastructure
visualIdeas: a city scene with traffic, smog and an overflowing garbage dump

topics.title: Planning Our Cities
objectives: Student can explain what urban planners must consider, such as transport, housing, green spaces and public facilities
Student can suggest ways to make a city sustainable and liveable
visualIdeas: a planned neighbourhood map with parks, schools, transit and homes

chapters.title: Cultural Currents: 13th to 17th Centuries
chapters.book: Exploring Society: India and Beyond Part 2

topics.title: Belief Systems and the Bhakti Tradition
objectives: Student can explain how Indian culture endured and grew richer during this period
Student can explain the bhakti marga as a path of devotion that did not require rituals or priests
visualIdeas: a map of India with bhakti saints placed in their regions

topics.title: Regional Saints and their Messages
objectives: Student can describe the messages of saints such as Kabir and Ravidas on equality and oneness
Student can explain how Sufi saints formed a bridge between cultures
visualIdeas: short couplets of Kabir and Ravidas on a scroll

topics.title: Musical Traditions — Continuation and Evolution
objectives: Student can describe how Indian music evolved while keeping its identity
Student can name the two streams of classical music, Hindustani and Carnatic
visualIdeas: a sitar and a veena side by side

topics.title: From Walls to Paper — Miniature Paintings
objectives: Student can explain how painting moved from walls to paper
Student can describe Rajput and Mughal miniature painting traditions
visualIdeas: a Rajput miniature beside a Mughal miniature

topics.title: Changing Landscapes — Gardens
objectives: Student can describe gardens in ancient Indian texts
Student can describe the Mughal charbagh garden design
visualIdeas: a charbagh garden plan with four parts and water channels

topics.title: Women in Society — Contextual Variations in Their Role and Status
objectives: Student can explain how the role and status of women varied by context during this period
Student can describe women who took part in public life, such as Razia Sultan and Nur Jahan, and the roles of women in south India such as at Vijayanagara
visualIdeas: Razia Sultan in her darbar beside Nur Jahan

topics.title: Education and Knowledge Traditions
objectives: Student can describe institutions of learning such as gurukulas, mathas, temple schools and pathshalas
Student can describe vocational education through the example of Banaras silk weaving and its brocades
visualIdeas: a weaver at a loom teaching an apprentice

topics.title: Growth of Literature and Language
objectives: Student can describe the flourishing of literature in many Indian languages
Student can explain how Urdu developed from Hindavi with Arabic and Persian words
visualIdeas: a map of languages with a sample word in each script

topics.title: Developments in Science and Technology
objectives: Student can describe Indian advances in science and technology during this period
Student can explain India's culture of enquiry and openness to other cultures
visualIdeas: an astronomical instrument of the period

topics.title: Regional Architectural Developments
objectives: Student can describe regional architecture such as the Konark Surya Mandir and Ranakpur temple
Student can describe temple building and reconstruction, for example at Hampi and Srirangam
visualIdeas: the stone wheels of the Konark Surya Mandir

topics.title: Cultural Exchange in Daily Life
objectives: Student can describe the two-way exchange in food and cuisine
Student can describe changes in clothing such as the jama and pyjama
visualIdeas: a Mughal-era kitchen and a painting of court clothing
